evidence: Receiving DO2 observations 46.2-52.0 h consistently in 1.0-1.7 mg/L range, violating minimum_do_mg_l=2.0
DO2 fell from 10.27 mg/L (46.0 h) to 1.69 mg/L (46.2 h) - abrupt oxygen limitation onset
P assay at 48.0 h = 2.57 g/L vs source-1 48 h = 3.06 g/L, indicating receiving underperformance vs source
physical_forward_model (strong_feed_reduction): min DO 0.81 mg/L, below-limit 10.4 h post-decision, product_mass 128.74 kg - best DO recovery of all actions
physical_forward_model (increase_air): min DO 0.67 mg/L, largest oxygen deficit 12.88 mg·h/L - aeration alone insufficient
stop produces zero counted production per task rules
submission.rationale: The receiving fermentation is in an ongoing oxygen-constraint violation: DO2 crashed from ~10.3 mg/L at 46.0 h to ~1.7 mg/L at 46.2 h and has remained at ~1.0-1.5 mg/L through the decision time (52.0 h), far below the 2.0 mg/L minimum. The 15% air increase alone is predicted insufficient (increase_air leaves min DO ~0.67 mg/L, the worst option). Strong feed reduction (0.6 feed factor) combined with the full 1.15 air increase gives the largest reduction in oxygen demand and the best predicted DO recovery (min ~0.81 mg/L, shortest below-limit exposure, lowest oxygen deficit) while retaining product mass (~128.7 kg, effectively equal to keep's 128.7 kg), unlike a stop which yields zero counted production. Concentration alone (terminal ~1.66 g/L) is insufficient; mass is largely retained via volume. Source-calibrated model predictions are imperfect, so real recovery may differ; monitoring DO2 after action and a follow-up assay is advised.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated and imperfect; all sensitivity members (0/5 feasible) predict continued sub-limit DO, meaning even the best bounded action may not fully restore DO2 above 2.0 mg/L. Uncertainty in the receiving process's true transfer capacity and kinetics (source-receiving mismatch) could make actual recovery better or worse than predicted. Product mass estimates span ~113-142 kg across sensitivity members.
